intro.heading: Handling events
intro.summary: The event loop lets your app respond to window close requests, key presses, and mouse movement.
polling.heading: Poll for events
polling.paragraph: Platform.pollEvent(event) returns true while there are events in the queue. Handle them inside your main loop.
polling.title: Avoid busy-waiting
polling.paragraph2: The example uses Platform.delay(8) because it does no rendering. Apps that render may structure the loop and handle synchronization differently.
types.heading: Common events
types.row.EventType-Quit.description: The operating system requested that the app quit.
types.row.EventType-WindowState.descript: Window close, resize, and other window changes.
types.row.EventType-KeyDown.description: Key press. You can also read scanCode.
listeners.heading: Watch for events
listeners.paragraph: addEventWatchListener() can deliver events directly on the SDL thread that produces them. This is useful for some integrations, but you need to synchronize access to shared data.
listeners.title: Keep draining the event queue
listeners.paragraph2: Even with an event watch, keep calling pollEvent() or processEvents() to update state and drain the queue.
